summary: Selected traffic now has a real 3D altitude path on the Flight Deck globe, with detailed type artwork at the top, a ground shadow beneath, and the live callsign and flight level attached to the aircraft.
releaseNotes: The selected aircraft's recorded trail now rises from the ground as a translucent 3D altitude curtain, with an altitude-coloured top edge and a faint ground trace.
The selected aircraft rides at the top of that path as its detailed type silhouette, turned to its live heading with a callsign and flight-level badge.
The aircraft's surface position remains a subdued detailed shadow inside an amber anchor ring, joined to the airborne marker by a dashed stalk.
Traffic now uses the detailed aircraft artwork from the chart atlas, with a neutral detailed fallback for types that have no dedicated sprite.
The selected path includes the aircraft's current position and altitude, so the 3D marker sits on the live target instead of stopping at the last polled sample.
The ground shadow suppresses its own map label, leaving one callsign on the airborne marker and no duplicate target below.
The marker, badge and altitude curtain follow the same camera as the globe through pitch, rotation and zoom.
Selected traffic no longer leaves the callsign and aircraft on the ground while its recorded path is elevated; the airborne marker and ground anchor now separate the two.
Aircraft types missing from the sprite atlas now use the detailed neutral silhouette rather than the simple legacy shape.
Traffic icons are cached per aircraft type, and the selected 3D path is redrawn only when the camera or selected samples change.
The 3D path uses the existing instrument palette: cyan and amber rings, an altitude-coloured edge, and a compact callsign and flight-level badge.
The 3D path is built only from observed traffic samples; a filed route remains a flat planned line because it carries no observed altitude profile.
